description: The first graded Solidity fixture (#6424). Two files are verbatim MIT OpenZeppelin v5.0.2 (Ownable.sol, ShortStrings.sol); two are hand-written on ordinary OZ shapes (MyToken.sol, Vault.sol) because no OZ file in reach carries a base-constructor `is` clause or a Yul function. See NOTICE.md. THIS FIXTURE IS DELIBERATELY RED. expected_entities and expected_relationships record what the extractor SHOULD produce, not what it does; six of the seven defects named in #6423 and #6425 are encoded here as must-haves that currently miss, and internal/quality/golden/baseline.json records the resulting sub-100% floor, which is the mechanism the ratchet already uses for csharp-aspnet-core-mini. Do NOT delete a must-have to make the fixture green -- fix #6423/#6425 and the floor rises. The seventh defect (the phantom Yul operation, #6425) is present in the source and measured in the issue thread but is NOT encoded here: forbidden_relationships hits are unconditionally fatal in scripts/quality/ratchet.py, so a currently-violated forbidden entry would break the gate rather than record a gap. NOTICE.md carries the exact entries to add once #6425 lands.

expected_entities.name: Ownable
expected_entities.note: `abstract contract Ownable is Context` -- the `abstract` prefix must not leak into the name or the subtype. WORKS today.

expected_entities.name: Ownable.owner
expected_entities.note: Members are owner-qualified. WORKS today.

expected_entities.name: Ownable._transferOwnership
expected_entities.note: Leading-underscore name. WORKS today.

expected_entities.name: Ownable.OwnershipTransferred
expected_entities.note: `event` declaration -- SCOPE.Operation subtype=event. WORKS today.

expected_entities.name: Ownable.onlyOwner
expected_entities.note: `modifier` DECLARATION. The declaration works today; its two USAGES do not -- see the relationship expectations.

expected_entities.name: Ownable._owner
expected_entities.note: Contract-level state variable. WORKS today (#6135).

expected_entities.name: Ownable.constructor
expected_entities.note: RED (#6423). `constructor(address initialOwner)` emits nothing: functionRE requires the literal `function` keyword and `constructor` sits in the CALLS denylist. In OpenZeppelin-shaped code the constructor is where the wiring happens. THE NAME IS THIS FIXTURE'S PROPOSAL, not a pre-existing convention -- the owner-qualified `Ownable.constructor` matches how every other member here is named. If #6423 lands on a different name, AMEND THIS ENTRY; do not rename the emitted entity to keep the fixture green.

expected_entities.name: Ownable.OwnableUnauthorizedAccount
expected_entities.note: RED (#6423). Contract-level `error OwnableUnauthorizedAccount(address account);` -- same defect class as ShortStrings.StringTooLong. Asserted so the `error` shape is scored over EVERY declaration the fixture's source contains, not a sample of them: a partial `error` fix cannot look complete.

expected_entities.name: Ownable.OwnableInvalidOwner
expected_entities.note: RED (#6423). Contract-level `error OwnableInvalidOwner(address owner);` -- same defect class.

expected_entities.name: ShortStrings
expected_entities.note: `library` declaration. WORKS today.

expected_entities.name: ShortStrings.toString
expected_entities.note: Contains an `assembly { }` block with no Yul function -- the declaration itself must survive it. WORKS today.

expected_entities.name: ShortStrings.FALLBACK_SENTINEL
expected_entities.note: `bytes32 private constant` with a 32-byte hex initializer. WORKS today.

expected_entities.name: ShortStrings.StringTooLong
expected_entities.note: RED (#6423). Contract-level `error StringTooLong(string str);` -- no code path emits `error` anywhere in the extractor. Modelled on `event`, which IS emitted as SCOPE.Operation, because the two share a shape: a named, parameterised, bodiless declaration that call sites reference by name.

expected_entities.name: ShortStrings.InvalidShortString
expected_entities.note: RED (#6423). Contract-level `error InvalidShortString();` -- a parameterless error, the same defect class as its parameterised sibling one line above it.

expected_entities.name: ShortString
expected_entities.note: RED (#6423). File-level `type ShortString is bytes32;` -- a user-defined value type, never emitted. It is a type declaration, so SCOPE.Schema, alongside struct and enum.

expected_entities.name: Vault
expected_entities.note: Plain `is Ownable` clause. WORKS today -- the contrast against MyToken below is what isolates the base-constructor-argument defect.

expected_entities.name: Vault.deposit
expected_entities.note: Carries a modifier usage in its signature. The declaration works; the usage edge does not.

expected_entities.name: Vault.roundUp
expected_entities.note: Body holds the `assembly { function helper(x) -> y ... }` block. The enclosing function must survive; the Yul function inside it must NOT become an entity -- see NOTICE.md, that half is not gateable today.

expected_entities.name: Vault.whenOpen
expected_entities.note: Modifier declaration. WORKS today.

expected_entities.name: Vault._deposits
expected_entities.note: `mapping(address => Deposit) private` -- the fat arrow must not be read as an initializer.

expected_entities.name: IERC20
expected_entities.note: `interface` declaration following a contract in the same file.

expected_entities.name: IERC20.transfer
expected_entities.note: Bodiless interface member terminated by ';' -- it must be an Operation, not a state variable (#6135).

expected_entities.name: Vault.constructor
expected_entities.note: RED (#6423). Same defect as Ownable.constructor, on a contract that IS otherwise extracted -- so this one is a member-level loss, not collateral damage from a contract that vanished.

expected_entities.name: Vault.receive
expected_entities.note: RED (#6423). `receive() external payable` -- the ether-receiving entry point of the contract, and invisible.

expected_entities.name: Vault.fallback
expected_entities.note: RED (#6423). `fallback() external payable` -- same mechanism.

expected_entities.name: computeFee
expected_entities.note: RED (#6423). File-level (free) function. Not owner-qualified because it has no owner; findContracts only walks matched contract bodies, so nothing outside one is ever scanned.

expected_entities.name: VaultState
expected_entities.note: RED (#6423). File-level `enum`. SCOPE.Schema follows the C#/VB.NET extractors, which both emit Enum as SCOPE.Schema.

expected_entities.name: Deposit
expected_entities.note: RED (#6423). File-level `struct`, and the value type of Vault._deposits.

expected_entities.name: VaultLocked
expected_entities.note: RED (#6423). File-level `error`. Reverted from both fallback() and the whenOpen modifier.

expected_entities.name: Vault.Receipt
expected_entities.note: RED (#6423). Contract-level `struct`, owner-qualified. Pins that the fix must cover BOTH positions -- a file-level-only fix would score on Deposit and still miss this.

expected_entities.name: Vault.Tier
expected_entities.note: RED (#6423). Contract-level `enum`, same reasoning.

expected_entities.name: Vault.VaultEmpty
expected_entities.note: RED (#6423). Contract-level `error VaultEmpty();` -- the contract-level counterpart of the file-level `VaultLocked` above, so a file-level-only `error` fix cannot score the class.

expected_entities.name: MyToken
expected_entities.note: RED (#6423), and the headline one. `contract MyToken is ERC20("My Token", "MTK")` -- contractRE renders the inheritance list as [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_,\s]* which cannot contain '(', so the declaration matches nothing and the contract is absent, not degraded.

expected_entities.name: MyToken.mint
expected_entities.note: RED (#6423), collateral. An ordinary function that would be extracted anywhere else; it is lost only because findContracts walks matched contract bodies and MyToken's never matched.

expected_entities.name: MyToken.Minted
expected_entities.note: RED (#6423), collateral -- an ordinary event.

expected_entities.name: MyToken.cap
expected_entities.note: RED (#6423), collateral -- an ordinary public state variable.

expected_entities.name: MyToken.constructor
expected_entities.note: RED twice over: lost to the vanished contract (#6423) AND to the constructor denylist (#6423). Fixing only contractRE will not score this point.

expected_relationships.note: Contract owns its functions. WORKS today.
Contract owns its state variables. WORKS today.
Interface owns its members. WORKS today.
In-tree inheritance across files, plain `is` clause. WORKS today.

External parent -- Context.sol is not in the fixture, so the resolver folds the bare `is Context` target onto a SCOPE.External node. THIS TARGET FOLDS, MOST DO NOT: counted in the emitted graph.json, only 3 entities are SCOPE.External (Context, encode, type) while 26 relationships still carry a RAW STRING ToID (computeFee, _msgSender, abi.encode, ShortString.wrap, add, wrap, getStringSlot, ...). to_name + to_kind is correct here BECAUSE Context folded; for an unresolved target to_bare_name is the correct and only way to assert the shape. See the `to_bare_name` note in NOTICE.md.
`owner() != _msgSender()` -- a bare parenthesised call resolved to the sibling method. WORKS today.

RED (#6423), and it fails on the TARGET rather than the source: the edge `Vault.deposit -> computeFee` is emitted today as a bare unresolved name, because the free function it names is never extracted. This is the pair that shows the free-function gap costs resolution, not just an entity count.

RED (#6423). Modifier USAGE: `function deposit(uint256 amount) public whenOpen`. declBody jumps from the parameter list's ')' straight to the body's '{', so everything between -- visibility, mutability, and every modifier invocation -- is never read. Modifiers are declared and contained, never connected to what uses them. CALLS is this fixture's proposal for the edge kind; a modifier usage is an invocation. If #6423 lands a distinct kind (USES/DECORATES), AMEND THIS ENTRY.

RED (#6423). The same modifier-usage gap, but with the modifier INHERITED from a base contract in another file -- so a fix that only looks for a modifier declared in the same body will score the Vault.whenOpen point above and still miss this one.

GREEN since #6423. The base name must survive the argument list: `is ERC20("My Token", "MTK")` extends ERC20, and the comma inside the argument list must not split the inheritance list into `ERC20(` and `)`. AMENDED when #6423 landed, on this file's own to_bare_name rule and NOTICE.md's instruction to amend an entry whose shape the fixture was PROPOSING rather than reporting. The original entry guessed `to_name: ERC20` + `to_kind: SCOPE.External`, which could not be measured at the time because MyToken did not exist at all. It is now measured and the guess was wrong: ERC20 does NOT fold to a SCOPE.External node -- ext-synthesis minted one for `Context` because that name is allowlisted, and renaming ERC20 to an arbitrary `Fooble`, or adding an arbitrary second parent to Ownable, produced no node either. So this target legitimately cannot resolve (ERC20 is a third-party base contract with no declaration in src/) and to_bare_name is the correct and only assertion for it. It is also the STRONGER of the two here: `to_name` on a non-existent entity can never pass, while the raw ToID comparison still fails if the parent is parsed as `ERC20(` or `)`, which is exactly the defect this entry exists to catch.

NICE-TO-HAVE, not a must-have, and deliberately so. `IERC20(token).transfer(to, total)` names the interface at the call site, and callBareRE (#6425) requires a LOWERCASE first character, so every capitalised bare target is dropped -- the under-fire half of the same call scan that over-fires on `type` and `abi.encode`. It is nice_to_have rather than must_exist because whether an explicit type conversion IS a call is a genuine design question, not a defect this fixture is entitled to settle; #6425 should decide it. What the entry does buy is that the decision becomes visible in the nice-to-have counters instead of invisible.

forbidden_relationships.note: Inheritance-direction guard. Vault extends Ownable, never the reverse; an inverted EXTENDS would still score full recall on the forward edge above.
`new string(32)` is a type instantiation, not an invocation of a function called `string`. Guards the denylist entry that keeps it out.
`emit Deposited(...)` -- the keyword must not be minted as a call target. The event reference itself is a separate question this fixture does not assert.
